name: Rottenmouth Viper
description:
When this creature enters the battlefield, [effect undetermined — see "Could not derive"].

Whenever this creature attacks, [effect undetermined — see "Could not derive"].
assumptions: Rendered the card's self-references as "this creature" (modern Magic templating), since the card's real name is withheld by design and no other self-reference convention is given in the packet.

Assumed standard trigger phrasing "When this creature enters the battlefield," and "Whenever this creature attacks," for the `trigger-type: "enter"` and `trigger-type: "attack"` nodes (C and E) — the schema names these trigger types but doesn't give literal wording, so I used the conventional Magic phrasing for each.

Treated nodes A (cast) and B (enters) as pure game mechanics (casting the spell, it entering the battlefield) rather than printed text, since neither carries any flags (e.g. `tapped`) that would generate an oracle-text clause.
couldNotDerive: The actual effect of the two `modifier` nodes (D, following the ETB trigger C; F, following the attack trigger E) — both carry `cond:delta=BLIGHT`. "BLIGHT" doesn't match any entry in the `labels` or `actions` registries, and it doesn't follow the documented delta formats shown in the schema (e.g. `delta=+1/+1`, `state=tapped`). So while the structure tells me self is modified once on ETB and again on every attack, I cannot determine what that modification actually is (a counter type and count, a stat change, a keyword grant, etc.) — I did not invent a plausible-sounding value for it.

Whether the two `delta=BLIGHT` modifications are identical in magnitude/kind or merely share the same label — the packet reuses the same flag string in both places, but nothing confirms they must be numerically identical rather than just the same category of effect.
Rarity — explicitly withheld by the packet.
Supertype (if any) — not present in the self registry's type line and not determinable from the nodes.
notes:
Confirmed via forge-model/data/rottenmouth-viper.txt: Name Rottenmouth Viper, ManaCost 5 B, Types Creature Elemental Snake, PT 6/6. Oracle: 'As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may sacrifice any number of nonland permanents. This spell costs {1} less to cast for each permanent sacrificed this way.\nWhenever Rottenmouth Viper enters or attacks, put a blight counter on it. Then for each blight counter on it, each opponent loses 4 life unless that player sacrifices a nonland permanent or discards a card.' Mana cost, type line, and P/T all reconstructed correctly. Verdict is issues-open on two distinct decomposition gaps in edges.json (not schema gaps, not agent misinterpretation — the examiner correctly refused to invent anything it couldn't see):

1. MISSING ADDITIONAL COST / COST REDUCTION. Node A (cast, from:hand, thing:self) carries no flags at all. The real card's cast has a variable additional cost: `A:SP$ PermanentCreature | Cost$ 5 B Sac<X/Permanent.nonLand/nonland permanent> | AILogic$ SacToReduceCost`, paired with a static ability `S:Mode$ ReduceCost | ValidCard$ Card.Self | Type$ Spell | Amount$ X | EffectZone$ All | Relative$ True` keyed to `SVar:X:Count$xPaid` — i.e. 'as an additional cost to cast this spell, you may sacrifice any number of nonland permanents; this spell costs {1} less for each permanent sacrificed this way.' This entire clause (an optional, unbounded-quantity sacrifice as part of the cast, feeding a scaler that reduces the printed mana cost by {1} per permanent) is absent from node A and from the flow entirely — there is no companion move/source node (owner:me, bf->gy, thing:any coarse-type or 'nonland permanent', flags 'may qty:0..N') feeding a cost-reduction scaler on A. Since the packet gave the examiner nothing to go on here, it correctly reported {5}{B} (the printed cost) without noticing the alternate-cost mechanic was missing — it had no way to know to look for it.

2. MISSING 'FOR EACH COUNTER, OPPONENT LOSES LIFE UNLESS...' CONSEQUENCE CHAIN. Nodes D and F (modifier, cond:delta=BLIGHT, downstream of enter-trigger C and attack-trigger E respectively) are both leaves in flow.steps — nothing follows either of them. In the real card, `SVar:TrigPutCounter:DB$ PutCounter | CounterType$ BLIGHT | CounterNum$ 1 | SubAbility$ DBRepeat` is only the first half of the triggered ability. `SubAbility$ DBRepeat` chains into `SVar:DBRepeat:DB$ Repeat | MaxRepeat$ Y` where `SVar:Y:Count$CardCounters.BLIGHT` (repeat once per blight counter currently on the creature), and each repetition runs `SVar:RepeatTorment:DB$ GenericChoice | Defined$ Opponent | Choices$ SacNonland,Discard` — each opponent independently chooses between `SVar:SacNonland:DB$ LoseLife | LifeAmount$ 4 | UnlessCost$ Sac<1/Permanent.nonLand>` and `SVar:Discard:DB$ LoseLife | LifeAmount$ 4 | UnlessCost$ Discard<1/Card>` (both 'lose 4 life unless...'), with `SVar:LoseLifeFallback` as the no-legal-cost fallback. None of this — the counter-count scaler (reading the just-placed BLIGHT counter total), the per-opponent 4-life-loss emit, or the sac-nonland-or-discard 'unless' combine('any') group — has any nodes anywhere in the packet. This is the single largest missing piece of the card (arguably its whole payoff), and it's missing identically on both the enter-trigger branch (after D) and the attack-trigger branch (after F). The examiner correctly flagged that it couldn't determine what D/F's delta=BLIGHT even meant, but the true gap is larger than that: the counter-placement fact is present (in mangled form, see #3), but its entire downstream consequence clause is absent from the decomposition, on both triggers.

3. SECONDARY/MINOR: node D and F's `cond:delta=BLIGHT` notation doesn't match any documented `cond:` delta format in SCHEMA.md (stat deltas like `delta=+1/+1`, or state changes like `state=tapped`/`state=untapped`), and 'BLIGHT' isn't a key in the `labels` registry. SCHEMA.md's own `emit` role description cites 'a lore counter added' as a canonical emit example, suggesting a named counter-type addition like this one belongs in `labels` (e.g. a `blight-counter` entry) referenced from an `emit` node, rather than encoded as a free-text `delta=` value on a `modifier` node. This ambiguity is exactly why the examiner could infer 'self changes twice' (right shape) but not name the change (counter add) — worth raising as a modeling-convention question for SCHEMA.md/REVIEW_PROCESS.md, secondary to gaps 1 and 2.

For the forgeTranslate.ts bug-fixing pass: the translator needs to (a) recognize `Cost$ ... Sac<X/...>` paired with `AILogic$ SacToReduceCost` and a `Mode$ ReduceCost` static keyed to `Count$xPaid` as a real additional-cost + cost-reduction edge pair on the cast node, and (b) recognize the `SubAbility$` chain from a `DB$ PutCounter` into `DB$ Repeat` (MaxRepeat tied to `Count$CardCounters.<TYPE>`) into `DB$ GenericChoice`/`UnlessCost$`-bearing `DB$ LoseLife` branches, translating it into a scaler (counter count) + emit (life loss) + combine('any') ('unless' cost choice) chain following the counter-add node — currently it appears to translate only the bare `PutCounter` fact and silently drop the entire `SubAbility$` continuation, on both the ChangesZone and Attacks trigger variants.
